Subject: Dedicated capacity guidance for launch (initial data attached)

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this. We attached a brief showing our expected traffic profile for the pilot (avg 850 qps across 3 endpoints, 1.1k token average per request during peak, long-tail 95th at ~2.2k tokens). We need recommendations on:

- SKU mix to hit a 95th-percentile latency SLO of ~300ms for the chat endpoint
- how to minimize committed spend while keeping predictable availability during our launch window
- fallback/failover plan if we go beyond committed capacity

Also included is a column with sensitive model sizes (we plan to serve a 70B dense model quantized, and a 13B distilled model for cheaper paths).

Attachments: blueharbor_capacity_request.pdf, throughput_modeling.xlsx

Can we get a short runbook and recommended reserved mix? Mike

Mike — thanks for the packet, that helps. High level before we dig into numbers:

- For your 70B quantized workload that needs tight tail latency, we'll recommend a mixed strategy: reserve a base of A100-class capacity for steady traffic, provision a small H100 reserve (canary/burst) for latency-sensitive spikes and slow-path completions, and use L4s for the distilled/cheap endpoints and embedding/async workloads.

- Key tradeoffs you should expect: H100 (best single-request latency and large memory headroom) is the most expensive per-hour; A100 gives high throughput per-dollar for batched steady-state; L4 is cost-efficient for small models and unbatched requests.

I'll loop Dev and Marissa to attach a quick sensitivity runbook with concrete numbers (qps -> reserved units mapping, and a canary plan). Can you confirm target steady qps (post-warmup) vs peak burst qps and what percent of traffic must maintain the 300ms 95th SLO?

—Jordan

Adding a technical note and a first-pass sensitivity table — high level numbers only here, full spreadsheet attached to thread.

Assumptions:
- Workload: 70B quantized model (~25–30GB VRAM working set with KV cache + activation overhead when using 4-bit quantization), 13B distilled model (~10GB working set)
- Typical batch behavior: chat endpoint will see small batches (1–4) for interactive flows; async endpoint batches to 16–32 for throughput ops
- Target SLO: 95th < 300ms for interactive chat flows, best-effort for async ops

SKU baseline performance (ballpark):
- H100 (80GB): best single-request latency for large models; supports large KV caches and long-sequence unbatched requests. For the 70B quantized model expect ~1.8–2.4x better 95th latency vs A100 on identical codepaths when heavily memory constrained.
- A100 (80GB): strong when you can batch; best $/token for steady, batched throughput. 95th latency will be higher than H100 for unbatched long sequences but comparable for batched workloads.
- L4 (24GB): cost-efficient for smaller models (13B) and embedding/assistant routes; limited for 70B unless heavily quantized and sharded.

First-pass reserved recommendation for pilot (steady state ~850 qps, peak bursts to ~1.6k qps):
- Reserve: 8 A100 (80GB equivalent) nodes for main steady throughput (covers ~70–75% of steady qps with batching)
- Reserve: 2 H100 nodes as latency reserve/canary (handles 10–15% of critical unbatched traffic + fast recovery for cold starts)
- Reserve: 4 L4 nodes for distilled model endpoints, embeddings, and background jobs

Rationale: The A100 pool handles most of the cost-effective capacity; H100s are there to protect 95th tail and to run the largest model paths during spikes. L4s handle cheap paths and reduce cost for non-critical traffic.

Autoscaling & fallback rules (can be codified in route policies):
- Primary: route interactive sessions to A100 until queue latency exceeds 120ms; then start spilling a weighted portion to H100 canary instances (20–30% of new sessions).
- If total CPU/GPU utilization > 78% across A100 pool for >2 mins, scale up A100s by +2 nodes (subject to burst limits) and increase H100 spill ratio.
- If we exhaust burst capacity, fall back to quantized 4-bit A100 model variants that reduce memory and increase throughput (degraded-quality path).

Cost/commit guidance: commit to the 8 A100s + 4 L4s for a 12-month window to get favorable pricing; keep H100s as short-term reserved or burstable add-on (monthly) unless BlueHarbor requires strict 95th SLOs under heavy load.

I'll attach the throughput_modeling.xlsx with per-SKU qps-to-node mapping.

—Dev

Short commercial notes to go with Dev's technical plan:

- Pricing: the recommended commit (8 A100 + 4 L4) moves BlueHarbor into a predictable monthly commit. We should propose a 12-month term with a 10% discount if they take H100 burst as a monthly add-on vs reserving H100s long-term.
- SLA/ops: include a 2-hour on-call for P1s during the 8-week launch window; offer an optional 99.9% availability SLA on reserved A100s for an additional fee.
- Contract language: add a clause to allow temporary burst above committed units for up to 20% of peak once per month (capacity hedging), charged at a pre-agreed overage rate.

I'll draft a short Commercial Attachment and send to legal; Jordan, please confirm if the October start date in their doc is the target (we need time for capacity provisioning + canary run).

—Marissa
